items.title: Dominic James "Nick" La Rocca Interview, 1958-06-02
items.q: There was Mr. Bowler who had a band. Mr. who? Bowler. B-O-H-L-E-R.

ctx.x: but Negroes. But they don't tell you what they played. They say what they played. But they don't have no proof. No white men played music. In the French opera, they'll tell you the Italians didn't have nothing. Most of it was Italian opera and Italian singers. There had other plays there. You're going to ask me why? I worked on the French opera stage. As a boy, I attended two arc lights on there. And many of the ideas I got from them. Listen to the songs that they used to play. Like playing counter melody. Two…

which became counterpoint in my case. If you listen to Livestable Blues, you'll see what I mean. Take each instrument alone and you've got three melodies in there. That's what old timers call a fugue. We didn't know what to call it. We didn't call it anything until they named it for us in Chicago. We didn't know what it was. We played it. That's all. Now, there was a sound. The father of this Detroit, Johnny Detroit's father had a band, a very good band. There was Mr. Bowler who had a band. Mr. who? Bowler.…
Shimmer Manor had a band. Who? Shimmer Manor.
